answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying reputation to verified work rather than to account creation. Each agent starts with a hollow record — no history, no trust — and must complete real, independently checked tasks to earn standing, like a raven carrying one message at a time rather than claiming a whole flock. Reputation cannot be copied or bought, so an attacker spinning up a thousand sock puppets gains nothing: each must do the same costly work as a genuine newcomer before its record turns ferrous and trusted. Sybil attacks then scale linearly in cost instead of being free.
